title: Sovereign Space ATLAS, Friday the twenty-seventh of November
headline: Mexico asks the United States for talks over suspected SpaceX debris

global.title: Mexico asks the United States for talks over suspected SpaceX debris
global.summary: Mexico has asked the United States for talks about suspected SpaceX debris. The request was published on the twenty-sixth of November. A second report, at 00:26 on the twenty-seventh, says Mexico may impose sanctions on SpaceX. Neither headline says where the debris fell or which launch it came from. SpaceX has made no statement in the material available.
global.why: A state is treating debris from a commercial launch as a matter for government talks. Sanctions on a launch company would be a new step.
global.bar: Headlines only; debris location, launch and sanctions basis unknown.

global.title: United States approves SpaceX plan for a million data-centre satellites
global.summary: The United States has approved a SpaceX plan to put a million satellites in orbit as data centres. The approval was reported on the twenty-sixth of November. Astronomers in Spain say they are consternated. Academics in Australia caution against the proposed Starmind constellation. The conditions and timetable are not given in the headlines.
global.why: The approval opens the largest satellite filing yet to be cleared. It sets up objections from astronomers and other states.
global.bar: Conditions and launch schedule unknown; filed 26 November, this adds the objections.

global.title: NASA holds Moon base proposals open until the eighth of December
global.summary: NASA made its first Moon base contract awards on the ninth of November. Proposals for the next round are due on the eighth of December. The awards are described as major. No further award date has been published. The next date is the eighth of December.
global.why: Companies not yet awarded have a fixed deadline. The next round decides who joins the first group.
global.bar: Standing item; deadline from thread notes.

global.title: United Launch Alliance has not given a cause for the Vulcan Centaur failure
global.summary: A Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying Amazon satellites failed on the fifteenth of November. No cause has been published. No date for the next flight has been given. Amazon's own satellites also fly on Ariane 6. Ariane 6 launches next on the seventeenth of December.
global.why: Amazon's launch plan now leans more on Ariane 6. The cause decides how long Vulcan stays grounded.
global.bar: Headline only; 40 satellites per headline; cause and return unknown.

items.title: ESA releases the largest data set from its Gaia mission
items.summary: ESA released Gaia's largest-ever data set on the twenty-sixth of November. The release was streamed live. Earlier that week ESA reported that BepiColombo is safely in orbit at Mercury. Euclid also broke its own quasar record. Ariane 6 flies next on the seventeenth of December.
items.why: The release gives researchers a new catalogue to work from. ESA's launch and science calendar continues into December.
items.bar: ESA has no ISO3; headline-level on contents.

items.title: European Council President Costa asks for a budget deal in December
items.summary: Costa says the Union budget needs an agreement in December. Italian press says the budget is splitting Europe. German Chancellor Merz says there will be no summit on the twenty-seventh. He says he is confident of a deal by the end of the year. The vote of the tenth of November on ESA funding had no outcome, and the meeting in Rome is on the fifteenth of December.
items.why: The Union budget sets the frame for space spending. A missed December deadline would leave the Rome meeting without that frame.
items.bar: General budget, space share not stated; link to Rome is by timing only.

items.title: Ukraine reports further Starshield restrictions; SpaceX is silent
items.summary: Ukraine reported more restrictions on Starshield access on the twelfth of November. SpaceX has made no statement. Ukraine's hope for mid-2027 is unchanged. Lithuanian press is following Russia's search for a Starlink analogue. No date for a decision has been given.
items.why: Ukraine's military communications depend on access it does not control. Any change would come from SpaceX or Washington.
items.bar: Standing situation; no new event today.

items.title: Sweden's space agency sets Space Day for the eighteenth of February
items.summary: The Swedish National Space Agency will hold its next Space Day on the eighteenth of February, 2027. The date was announced on the second of November. The agency's November pages mark Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth. They also cover Hera's role in asteroid defence. The next date is the eighteenth of February.
items.why: Space Day is the agency's main yearly public event. It is a fixed point for Swedish space announcements.

items.title: Spanish astronomers object to SpaceX permission for a million satellites
items.summary: Astronomers have objected to the permission given to SpaceX for a million satellites. Spanish press quotes them as saying they are consternated. The permission came from the United States. Spain's own authorities have not been quoted. No date for any response has been given.
items.why: Astronomers are the first organised group to push back. European states may be asked to take a position.
items.bar: Regional reaction to the global item.

items.title: Armenia and SpaceX discuss Starlink and a possible launch of three satellites
items.summary: Armenia's regulator and SpaceX have discussed Starlink and mobile communications. Separate talks covered Grok in education. They also covered a possible launch of three satellites. No agreement has been announced. No date for a decision has been published.
items.why: Armenia is weighing a direct commercial link with SpaceX. It also signed a technology protocol with Iran.

items.title: Türkiye plans a new microsatellite for 2028 and a Turkic states satellite for 2027
items.summary: Türkiye's new microsatellite is due to launch in 2028. A joint satellite of the Turkic states is due in 2027. A trade report puts the proposed 2027 space budget at nine billion lira. It puts the figure over three years at ninety-two billion lira. No split has been published.
items.why: Türkiye is building both national and shared capacity. The budget split would show which program gets the money.
items.bar: Headline-level; budget figures via trade press, no split.

items.title: ESA waits for Australia to commit funding for the Bennell-Pegg flight
items.summary: ESA is waiting for an Australian funding commitment for Katherine Bennell-Pegg's spaceflight. Space Connect says the launch clock is ticking. No decision date has been given. Academics also caution against Musk's Starmind constellation. Australian press is covering the space race around Koonibba.
items.why: An Australian astronaut's flight depends on a government decision. The wait is now publicly reported.
items.bar: Headline-level; funding amount and deadline unknown.

items.title: Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every American child
items.summary: Elon Musk pledged two SpaceX shares for every American child on the twenty-sixth of November. The pledge was carried the same day. No mechanism has been described in the headlines. No date has been given. The same day, the United States approved the SpaceX satellite plan.
items.why: The pledge ties SpaceX's public standing to a mass shareholding. Terms are needed before it can be judged.
items.bar: Same wire counted once; terms unknown.

audio_script:
Good morning. It is Friday, the twenty-seventh of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Mexico has asked the United States for talks about suspected SpaceX debris. ESA has released the largest data set in the history of its Gaia mission. And Australia is waiting on a funding decision that ESA needs before an Australian astronaut can fly.

Mexico has asked the United States for talks about suspected SpaceX debris. The request was published on the twenty-sixth of November. A second report, from Azerbaijan's APA agency at 00:26 today, says Mexico may impose sanctions on SpaceX. Neither headline says where the debris fell, which launch it came from, or what sanctions are under consideration. SpaceX has made no statement in the material available this morning. Mexico has not given a date for the talks. The next step is whether Washington answers, and whether Mexico names a sanctions measure.

In Europe, ESA released Gaia's largest-ever data set on the twenty-sixth of November. The tenth Ariane 6 launched thirty-six Amazon Leo satellites on the twenty-fourth of November. The next Ariane 6 flies on the seventeenth of December, carrying the Metop-SGB1 weather satellite. The vote of the tenth of November produced no outcome, the MaiaSpace contract is unsigned, and the meeting in Rome is on the fifteenth of December. On the Union budget, European Council President Costa says an agreement is needed in December. German Chancellor Merz says there will be no summit today, and that he is confident of a deal by the end of the year.

In Ukraine, access to Starshield remains restricted. President Zelenskyy reported further restrictions on the twelfth of November. SpaceX has made no statement. Ukraine's hope for mid-2027 is unchanged.

In Sweden, the national space agency will hold its next Space Day on the eighteenth of February, 2027. The agency's November pages also mark Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth.

In Spain, astronomers have objected to the permission given to SpaceX for a million satellites. Spanish press quotes them as saying they are consternated. The permission came from the United States on the twenty-sixth of November. No date for any response has been given.

In Armenia, the public services regulator and SpaceX have discussed Starlink and mobile communications. Separate talks covered Grok in education and a possible launch of three satellites. No date for a decision has been published.

In Türkiye, a new microsatellite is due to launch in 2028, and a joint satellite of the Turkic states is due in 2027. A trade report puts the proposed space budget at nine billion lira for 2027, and ninety-two billion lira over three years. No split has been published.

In Australia, ESA is waiting for the government to commit funding for Katherine Bennell-Pegg's spaceflight. Space Connect says the launch clock is ticking. No decision date has been given. Separately, academics have cautioned against Musk's proposed Starmind constellation.

In the United States, SpaceX has been approved to put a million satellites in orbit as data centres. The conditions and timetable have not been published. On the twenty-sixth of November Musk also pledged two SpaceX shares for every American child. NASA's proposals for the next Moon base round are due on the eighth of December.

What we are tracking this week is whether the United States answers Mexico, and whether sanctions on SpaceX take a formal shape. We are also tracking any word on Australia's funding for the Bennell-Pegg flight, and a cause for the Vulcan Centaur failure of the fifteenth of November. What we are tracking this month: Moon base proposals, due on the eighth of December; the Rome meeting on the fifteenth of December; and the Ariane 6 launch of Metop-SGB1 on the seventeenth of December. Heads-up dates: Blue Origin's January return is unconfirmed, and Swedish Space Day is on the eighteenth of February. That is the briefing for Friday, the twenty-seventh of November. Thank you for listening.

A report from Azerbaijan says Mexico may impose sanctions on SpaceX.
ESA released the largest data set from its Gaia mission, and Australia's funding for an Australian astronaut's flight is awaited.
Astronomers in Spain have objected to the American approval of a million SpaceX satellites.

bottom_line: The Mexico and SpaceX debris dispute is at the stage of a request for talks, with no date set. The next fixed date that matters is the fifteenth of December in Rome.
